task_instruction:
Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi, my mobile data has been acting up — it either stops working completely or crawls at a snail's pace. I really need to get this sorted out.

turns.thought:

turns.thought:
Thanks, John — I've pulled up your account. Your line **555-123-2002 (Line L1002)** is **Active**, and your billing is in good standing (no overdue bills, so no suspension-related cutoff).

Your data usage is **8.7 GB out of 15 GB** for this cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28), so you haven't hit your plan's data limit — that rules out a cap-related slowdown.

Line: L1002 · Premium Plan · 15 GB limit · $65/mo

Since this looks like a device/network-side issue rather than an account-side one, I need a bit more detail before I can narrow it down:

1. **Are you currently traveling outside your home network area (e.g., abroad or in a rural/roaming region)?**
2. **Does the problem happen everywhere, or only in specific locations?**
3. **Does the total loss of data happen at particular times, or is it random?**

In the meantime, one thing worth confirming on your device: your line currently has **international/data roaming turned OFF** at the account level. If you're outside your home coverage area, that would cut your data off completely — and I can enable it for you at no cost.
turns.execution_output:
User: Yes — I'm actually abroad right now, in France. As for the rest, it seems pretty random; it's been happening since I arrived here, both when I'm out and about and back at the hotel. I don't have access to Wi-Fi, so I'm fully dependent on mobile data.

That roaming thing sounds like it could be exactly the problem — please go ahead and turn it on if you can.

turns.thought: That's very likely the root cause — your line has roaming disabled, and you're outside your home network. Let me enable it for you right now at no cost.

Confirmed — international roaming is now **enabled** on your line 555-123-2002 (verified: `roaming_enabled: true`), at no cost to you. That was almost certainly why your data was cutting out entirely while you're in France.

There's one more step on your phone itself, though. Account-level roaming lets the line connect to partner networks, but your device also has its own **Data Roaming** switch, and both need to be ON for data to work abroad. Since you have no Wi-Fi, this needs to happen on the device:

1. Open **Settings** → **Connections** (or **Network & Internet** / **Cellular**, depending on your model — you're on a Smartphone Pro Max)
2. Tap **Mobile Networks** (or **Cellular Data Options**)
3. Turn **Data Roaming** **ON**

Once that's on, please confirm whether data comes back. A couple of things to be aware of in case the connection is only slow rather than fully down:

- **Network mode**: Make sure your phone isn't locked to 2G/3G — set it to 4G/5G preferred.
- **Data Saver**: If it's on, it will throttle things and make apps feel unresponsive — worth turning off while traveling.
- **VPN**: If you have one connected, it can slow things dramatically; try disconnecting it.

Your data usage is 8.7 GB of your 15 GB limit this cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28), so you have headroom — a full cutoff from hitting your cap isn't the cause right now.

Turn Data Roaming on and let me know how it goes. If data still drops out or crawls, tell me what your signal bars show and I'll take it from there.

Yes — definitely turn Airplane Mode off. That's exactly why you're seeing "no service" with no signal.

While Airplane Mode is ON, it disconnects **all** of your phone's wireless radios — cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth — so it doesn't matter that your SIM is active, mobile data is enabled, and we've turned data roaming on. It blocks all of them at once.

**On your device:** Go to **Settings** → turn **Airplane Mode** **OFF**. (You can also just swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings and tap the airplane icon to toggle it off.)

Good news is the rest is already in place:
- SIM: **Active** ✓
- Mobile data: **Enabled** ✓
- Data Roaming: **ON** on the device ✓
- International roaming: **Enabled** on your line 555-123-2002 ✓

Once Airplane Mode is off, your phone should re-register on a French partner network. Give it a minute or two — reconnecting abroad can take a little longer than at home, and you should see the signal bars return.

If the signal comes back but data is still slow or drops, let me know what the signal strength looks like and whether you see a network type next to it (like 4G, LTE, or 5G), and I'll keep troubleshooting from there.

Yes — I'd recommend turning Data Saver off.

Here's why: Data Saver restricts background data usage to conserve data, and while roaming abroad it's one of the common causes of a connection feeling slow or apps appearing unresponsive — things like messaging, maps, and email refresh can stall or lag even though you have a strong 5G signal.

It's worth noting you have plenty of headroom — **8.7 GB used of your 15 GB limit**, with your cycle ending 2025-02-28 — so there's no need to be conserving data right now.

**On your device:** Go to **Settings** → **Connections** → **Data Usage** → **Data Saver** and turn it **OFF**. (On many phones you can also swipe down the Quick Settings panel and tap the Data Saver tile directly.)

Important clarification: turning off Data Saver won't increase what you're billed for while roaming beyond your normal usage — your 15 GB plan allowance stays the same. But do be aware that with Data Saver off, apps will now be free to use data in the background, so your usage will climb a bit faster than it has been. Given you're at 8.7 of 15 GB, that's manageable, but it's something to keep an eye on.

Also, one more thing worth checking since you mentioned depending entirely on mobile data: check whether you have a **VPN** connected. A VPN can slow your connection significantly, and if it's running, try disconnecting it to see if speeds improve.

Turn Data Saver off and let me know if the speed picks up.

You're very welcome — glad we got it sorted out, and thanks for your patience walking through the steps.

To recap what resolved it for your line **555-123-2002**:

1. **International roaming enabled** on your line (account-level) — at no cost, since you're in France ✓
2. **Airplane Mode turned OFF** — this was blocking all your wireless radios, which is why you had no service at all ✓
3. **Data Roaming turned ON** on the device ✓
4. **Data Saver turned OFF** — this was throttling your connection ✓

Result: 5G, excellent signal, 275 Mbps. 

A couple of notes for the rest of your trip:

- With Data Saver now off, apps can use data in the background, so your usage will climb faster. You're at **8.7 GB of your 15 GB** limit with the cycle ending **2025-02-28**. If you get close to the cap, data connectivity will cut off — at that point we can add up to 2 GB via a data refuel at $2.00/GB on your Premium Plan, or look at plan options. Just reach out.
- Your account is in good standing with no overdue bills, so nothing on the billing side will interrupt your service.

If anything changes while you're abroad — data drops again, or you hit your limit — message me any time. Safe travels!
